original_question: In the polynomial tuning construction, does the resulting tuned polynomial depend continuously on P1 when P1 is restricted to have a superstable orbit?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Question 7 in the tuning subsection of "Questions in Quasiconformal Surgery": the continuity of the tuning with respect to P1, under the paper's restriction to P1 of degree greater than 2 with a superstable orbit of fixed period. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the tuning construction, asks about continuity in the variable P1 rather than P2, and notices that the superstable-orbit restriction is part of the intended scope. That is the core content of Section 1, Question 7. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
missing_details: The paper fixes the auxiliary polynomial P2; the question is about varying P1 while holding P2 fixed. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

P1 is not arbitrary: it must have a periodic critical point ω of period k, and no other critical points may lie in the full basin of the associated superattracting cycle. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

P2 must have exactly one critical point, and the local degree of that critical point must match the local degree of ω. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

The setup assumes that the Julia sets of P1 and P2 are connected, that the closure of the immediate basin of ω is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk, and that the Julia set of P2 is locally connected. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

If the common critical degree d is greater than 2, one must choose one of the d−1 possible conjugating homeomorphisms between P1^k on the closed immediate basin and z ↦ z^d on the closed disk; this choice is part of the tuning data. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

Question 7 adds an extra restriction absent from the draft: only P1 of degree greater than 2 and with a superstable orbit of fixed period are considered. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

The paper phrases the output as the resulting tuning; nearby context says it should be conjugate to a polynomial, so the canonical object is the tuning construction itself rather than a specifically normalized polynomial representative. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
The ambient setting is complex polynomial dynamics, which the draft leaves implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9201271))

The paper does not spell out a normalization or topology for the continuity statement, so those should not be added as if they were part of the original formulation. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
refined_question: Fix a complex polynomial P2 whose Julia set is connected and locally connected and which has exactly one critical point of local degree d. Let P1 vary among complex polynomials of degree greater than 2 with connected Julia set, having a periodic critical point ω of fixed period k and local degree d, such that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle and the closure of the immediate basin of ω is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk; when d > 2, fix one of the possible conjugacies between P1^k on that closed basin and z ↦ z^d on the closed unit disk. For the tuning obtained by tuning P1 with P2 at ω, does the resulting tuning vary continuously as P1 varies within this family? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 1, Question 7, not Question 6 or Question 8. Question 6 asks whether the output varies continuously with P2, whereas Question 7 asks whether the tuning varies continuously with P1 under the restriction that P1 have degree greater than 2 and a superstable orbit of fixed period. Question 8 is a different limit problem in which the period of the superstable orbit tends to infinity. The refined version above imports only the hypotheses stated in the immediately preceding tuning setup and keeps the scope no broader than the paper. This paper is a problem list, so the nearest official formulation is a numbered question rather than a theorem, proposition, or conjecture. ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))
